Under normal market conditions, these tools handle routine rebalancing, such as automatically adjusting debt levels to keep constant leverage or smoothly scaling a position’s safety ratio from, for example, 180% to 200%.
However, during a major market selloff between January 25 and February 9, DeFi Saver’s system executed a total of 382 automated repay actions on Aave V3 alone.
Out of these, 95.55% were critical interventions executed on heavily exposed positions running a Safety ratio of <150% (Health factor of 1.55) - all of which would have faced certain liquidation during the event given the size of the market correction.
So today, in this study, we'll be looking at the 365 at-risk positions managed by DFS Automation between January 25 and February 9. To be more precise, these are Aave V3 positions managed via DeFi Saver, across Ethereum Mainnet, Base, Optimism, and Arbitrum.

🧠 Crypto News Brief: Self-custody took the hardest hit of the year as a five-year-old firmware flaw emptied hundreds of Coldcard wallets. Meanwhile, earnings season laid bare how deeply the Q2 drawdown cut into crypto's biggest balance sheets. 🔓 Coldcard Firmware Flaw Drains 594 BTC in a 25-Minute Sweep An attacker emptied roughly 500 single-signature Bitcoin wallets between 01:31 and 01:56 UTC, moving about 594 BTC — some $38 million — across 500 transactions inside a three-block window, then consolidating 562 BTC into a single address that has not moved since. Block's Bitcoin engineering team traced the cause to Coldcard firmware that had silently bypassed its dedicated hardware random number generator since March 2021, producing seeds weak enough to be guessed. Every drained wallet was created inside that window. Coinkite has shipped emergency patches and is urging affected holders to migrate funds. Read full story ⚖️ New York Sues Kalshi, Calling Prediction Markets "Gambling, Plain and Simple" Governor Kathy Hochul and Attorney General Letitia James filed suit in Manhattan state court alleging KalshiEX runs an unlicensed gambling business, seeking an injunction, forfeiture of profits, restitution for users and fines equal to three times the company's gains — exposure the state estimates could reach $36 billion. Kalshi dismissed the action as political theater, arguing states cannot shut down a federally licensed exchange. The CFTC has filed for a temporary restraining order to halt New York's case. More details 📉 Strategy Books $8.2 Billion Quarterly Loss on Bitcoin Markdown Michael Saylor's Strategy reported an $8.22 billion second-quarter net loss, driven almost entirely by an $8.32 billion unrealized markdown under fair-value accounting after bitcoin fell roughly 14% during the quarter. The firm holds 843,775 BTC worth about $54.8 billion against a $63.7 billion cost basis. It has built a $3.75 billion dollar reserve — enough to cover preferred dividends and interest for more than two years — and has started selling small tranches of bitcoin to fund them, a clear break from its buy-and-hold doctrine.
